before_source.text: ἐλάλησα; οὐ πάντοτέ σε ὡς θεὰν ἡγησάμην; οὐ πάντοτέ σε ἐνετράπην ὡς ἀδελφήν; τί μου καταψεύδῃ, ὦ γύναι, τὰ πονηρὰ ταῦτα καὶ ἀκάθαρτα; 8. γελάσασά μοι λέγει· Ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν σου ἀνέβη ἡ ἐπιθυμία τῆς πονηρίας. ἢ οὐ δοκεῖ σοι ἀνδρὶ δικαίῳ πονηρὸν πρᾶγμα εἶναι ἐὰν ἀναβῇ αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν ἡ πονηρὰ ἐπιθυμία; ἁμαρτία γέ ἐστιν, καὶ μεγάλη, φησίν. ὁ γὰρ δίκαιος ἀνὴρ δίκαια βουλεύεται. ἐν τῷ οὖν δίκαια βουλεύεσθαι αὐτὸν κατορθοῦται ἡ δόξα αὐτοῦ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς καὶ εὐκατάλλακτον ἔχει τὸν Κύριον ἐν παντὶ πράγματι αὐτοῦ· οἱ δὲ πονηρὰ βουλευόμενοι ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις αὐτῶν θάνατον καὶ αἰχμαλωσίαν ἑαυτοῖς ἐπισπῶνται, μάλιστα οἱ τὸν αἰῶνα τοῦτον περιποιούμενοι καὶ γαυριῶντες ἐν τῷ πλούτῳ αὐτῶν καὶ μὴ ἀντεχόμενοι τῶν ἀγαθῶν τῶν μελλόντων. 9. μετανοήσουσιν αἱ ψυχαὶ αὐτῶν, οἵτινες οὐκ ἔχουσιν ἐλπίδα, ἀλλὰ ἑαυτοὺς ἀπηγνώκασι καὶ τὴν ζωὴν αὐτῶν. ἀλλὰ σὺ προσεύχου πρὸς τὸν Θεόν, καὶ ἰάσεται τὰ ἁμαρτήματά σου καὶ ὅλου τοῦ οἴκου σου καὶ πάντων τῶν ἁγίων.

after_source.text: Ὁ θρέψας με πέπρακέν με Ῥόδῃ τινὶ εἰς Ῥώμην. μετὰ πολλὰ ἔτη ταύτην ἀνεγνωρισάμην καὶ ἠρξάμην αὐτὴν ἀγαπᾶν ὡς ἀδελφήν. 2. μετὰ χρόνον τινὰ λουομένην εἰς τὸν ποταμὸν τὸν Τίβεριν εἶδον, καὶ ἐπέδωκα αὐτῇ τὴν χεῖρα καὶ ἐξήγαγον αὐτὴν ἐκ τοῦ ποταμοῦ. ταύτης οὖν ἰδὼν τὸ κάλλος διελογιζόμην ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ μου λέγων· Μακάριος ἤμην εἰ τοιαύτην γυναῖκα εἶχον καὶ τῷ κάλλει καὶ τῷ τρόπῳ. μόνον τοῦτο ἐβουλευσάμην, ἕτερον δὲ οὐδὲ ἕν. 3. μετὰ χρόνον τινὰ πορευομένου μου εἰς Κώμας καὶ δοξάζοντος τὰς κτίσεις τοῦ Θεοῦ, ὡς μεγάλαι καὶ ἐκπρεπεῖς καὶ δυναταί εἰσιν, περιπατῶν ἀφύπνωσα. καὶ πνεῦμά με ἔλαβεν καὶ ἀπήνεγκέ με δι᾿ ἀνοδίας τινός, δι᾿ ἧς ἄνθρωπος οὐκ ἐδύνατο ὁδεῦσαι· ἦν δὲ ὁ τόπος κρημνώδης καὶ ἀπερρηγὼς ἀπὸ τῶν ὑδάτων. διαβὰς οὖν τὸν ποταμὸν ἐκεῖνον ἦλθον εἰς τὰ ὁμαλά, καὶ τιθῶ τὰ γόνατα καὶ ἠρξάμην προσεύχεσθαι τῷ Κυρίῳ καὶ ἐξομολογεῖσθαί μου τὰς ἁμαρτίας. 4. προσευχομένου δέ μου ἠνοίγη ὁ οὐρανός, καὶ βλέπω τὴν γυναῖκα ἐκείνην ἣν ἐπεθύμησα ἀσπαζομένην με ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, λέγουσαν· Ἑρμᾶ, χαῖρε. 5. βλέψας δὲ εἰς αὐτὴν λέγω αὐτῇ· Κυρία, τί σὺ ὧδε ποιεῖς; ἡ δὲ ἀπεκρίθη μοι· Ἀνελήφθην ἵνα σου τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἐλέγξω πρὸς τὸν Κύριον. 6. λέγω αὐτῇ· Νῦν σύ μου ἔλεγχος εἶ; Οὔ, φησίν, ἀλλὰ ἄκουσον τὰ ῥήματα ἅ σοι μέλλω λέγειν. ὁ Θεὸς ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς κατοικῶν καὶ κτίσας ἐκ τοῦ μὴ ὄντος τὰ ὄντα καὶ πληθύνας καὶ αὐξήσας ἕνεκεν τῆς ἁγίας ἐκκλησίας αὐτοῦ ὀργίζεταί σοι ὅτι ἥμαρτες εἰς ἐμέ. 7. ἀποκριθεὶς αὐτῇ λέγω· Εἰς σὲ ἥμαρτον; ποίῳ τρόπῳ; ἢ πότε σοι αἰσχρὸν ῥῆμα ἐλάλησα; οὐ πάντοτέ σε ὡς θεὰν ἡγησάμην; οὐ πάντοτέ σε ἐνετράπην ὡς ἀδελφήν; τί μου καταψεύδῃ, ὦ γύναι, τὰ πονηρὰ ταῦτα καὶ ἀκάθαρτα; 8. γελάσασά μοι λέγει· Ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν σου ἀνέβη ἡ ἐπιθυμία τῆς πονηρίας. ἢ οὐ δοκεῖ σοι ἀνδρὶ δικαίῳ πονηρὸν πρᾶγμα εἶναι ἐὰν ἀναβῇ αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν ἡ πονηρὰ ἐπιθυμία; before_text:
"Did I speak? Did I not always regard you as a goddess [1]? Did I not always respect you as a sister? Why are you falsely accusing me, woman, of these wicked and unclean things?"

She laughed and says to me, "Evil desire has risen up into your heart [2]. Or does it not seem to you a wicked thing for a righteous man if evil desire rises into his heart? It is indeed a sin—and a great one, she says. For a righteous man plans what is righteous. Therefore, in planning what is righteous, his honor is established in the heavens [3], and he has the Lord readily reconciled [4] in every affair of his. But those who plan evil in their hearts bring upon themselves death and captivity—especially those who secure this present age for themselves [5], who exult in their wealth, and who do not hold fast to the good things that are coming.

"Will their souls repent[a] [6]—those who have no hope, but have despaired of themselves and of their life? But you—pray to God, and he will heal your sins [7], and those of your whole household, and of all the holy ones [8]."
after_text:
I.1. The man who raised me sold me to a certain Rhoda in Rome[b]. After many years I came to know her again and began to love her as a sister.

I.2. Later I saw her bathing in the river Tiber. I gave her my hand and helped her out of the river. When I saw her beauty, I thought in my heart, "I would be happy if I had a wife like her, both in beauty and in character." That was all I considered, nothing more.

I.3. Some time later, as I was going to Cumae[c] and praising God's creations—how great, splendid, and powerful they are—I fell asleep while walking. A spirit took me and carried me along a pathless place where no one could walk. The place was steep and broken up by the waters. After crossing that river, I reached level ground, knelt down, and began to pray to the Lord and confess my sins.

I.4. While I was praying, heaven opened, and I saw the woman I had desired greeting me from heaven and saying, "Greetings, Hermas!"

I.5. I looked at her and said, "Lady, what are you doing here?" She answered me, "I was taken up to expose your sins before the Lord."

I.6. I said to her, "Are you now my accuser?" "No," she said, "but listen to what I am about to tell you. God, who lives in the heavens and created what exists out of what did not exist, who multiplied it and made it grow for the sake of his holy church, is angry with you because you sinned against me."

I.7. I answered her, "Did I sin against you? In what way? Or when did I ever say anything shameful to you? Did I not always regard you as a goddess[1]? Did I not always respect you as a sister? Why are you falsely accusing me, woman, of these wicked and unclean things?"

I.8. She laughed and said to me, "Evil desire has risen up into your heart[2]. Or does it not seem to you[d] a wicked thing for a righteous man if evil desire rises into his heart? It is indeed a sin—and a great one. For a righteous man plans what is righteous. Therefore, in planning what is righteous, his honor is established in the heavens[3], and he has the Lord readily reconciled[4] in every affair of his. But those who plan evil in their hearts bring upon themselves death and captivity—especially those who secure this present age for themselves[5], who exult in their wealth, and who do not hold fast to the good things that are coming.

I.9. "Their souls will repent[a][6]—those who have no hope, but have despaired of themselves and of their life. But you—pray to God, and he will heal your sins[7], and those of your whole household, and of all the holy ones[8]."

translation.text:
"Did I speak? Did I not always regard you as a goddess [1]? Did I not always respect you as a sister? Why are you falsely accusing me, woman, of these wicked and unclean things?"

She laughed and says to me, "Evil desire has risen up into your heart [2]. Or does it not seem to you a wicked thing for a righteous man if evil desire rises into his heart? It is indeed a sin—and a great one, she says. For a righteous man plans what is righteous. Therefore, in planning what is righteous, his honor is established in the heavens [3], and he has the Lord readily reconciled [4] in every affair of his. But those who plan evil in their hearts bring upon themselves death and captivity—especially those who secure this present age for themselves [5], who exult in their wealth, and who do not hold fast to the good things that are coming.

"Will their souls repent[a] [6]—those who have no hope, but have despaired of themselves and of their life? But you—pray to God, and he will heal your sins [7], and those of your whole household, and of all the holy ones [8]."

footnotes.text: Repentance and related expressions are read in this works own context; they are not restricted to feeling sorry, and no uniform Godward formula is imposed. Use repentance for moral change while preserving the works own teaching about baptism, forgiveness, conduct and the angel of repentance; do not impose a different tradition on it.
